propositions: The wire history processor's context window check never executes on first requests because the filter predicate only descends into ModelResponse messages with failed output, and a first request history contains only ModelRequest, leaving the sole raise site (ContextWindowExceededError) unreachable.

Oversized first requests pass through to the provider (measured: 3.6M chars against 1M token window with guard invoked 0 times) and surface as LLMUnavailableError (provider-outage semantics) instead of a deterministic input-size error, masking caller-fixable problems.

A seam-level request-fit check requires three design decisions: (1) token estimation constant calibration (2 vs 4 chars/token affects whether enrich's window*2-char bound remains admissible), (2) posture choice (fail-closed shared error vs per-op catchable error), (3) convergence (per-op bounds as first-line vs deferred to seam backstop).
